Earlier this year, there were widespread market rumors that iOS 26.4 would bring a redesigned Health app. The project was subsequently delayed, and even after iOS 27 launched, some time has passed without the rewritten Health app ever making an appearance.

With the all-new Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 set to be unveiled next month, it's worth asking: will the related new features be announced at the same time?

Precedent

First, it's worth revisiting why these features are very likely to be announced in September. You might think: 'Shouldn't all software be unveiled in June?' — but there is indeed precedent in this regard.

Features such as Low Power Mode in watchOS 9, sleep apnea detection in watchOS 11, and hypertension notifications in watchOS 26 did not require the latest hardware to function, yet were all only formally announced in September.

Therefore, based on the reasons above, it is highly likely that Apple will wait until September to announce the latest Health app upgrades, even though these features do not necessarily require the all-new Apple Watch to use.

Still time

Before WWDC27, Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman warned that the Health app upgrade project, known as "Project Mulberry," might not make an appearance at the WWDC keynote. As it turned out, that was indeed the case:

Does this mean Project Mulberry is guaranteed to appear at the September event? Not necessarily. However, given that features have previously been announced in September, and we already knew the project might launch later than WWDC, the chances of a September unveiling look fairly high — even if it may ultimately arrive in October alongside iOS 27.1.

Feature recap

Due to the many factors involved, the related rumors have been all over the place. You may have heard that a standalone Health+ service would launch, accompanied by videos filmed by doctors. However, according to reports, the plans have been scaled back, with the relevant features instead being integrated into the existing Health app experience.

Nevertheless, two things are already fairly clear: first, an AI health coach will be introduced to provide health recommendations based on your Health app data; second, real-time guidance can be provided through the camera for exercise and other health-related tasks. Another key focus of this upgrade is that the Health app will feature a brand-new design, making it easier for users to understand the various data points.

Beyond that, we'll just have to wait and see. Personally, I'm very much looking forward to a better way to organize and understand my own Apple Health data.
